name: Wattle Hollow Retreat Center
tradition: Insight Meditation (Vipassana) in the Theravada tradition, offered alongside yoga, dance, and creative-arts retreats
technique: Theravada Vipassana practice: sitting meditation, walking meditation, mindful eating, and metta (loving-kindness) practice, observed in Noble Silence.
teacherAccess: Founder/director Joy Fox leads meditation instruction, group discussion periods, and sends an orientation letter before each retreat; other visiting teachers lead their own weekend yoga, Vajrayana, or music programs.
retreatOptions: Monthly one-day silent 'Dharma Days' (10am-4pm); periodic two-night weekend meditation retreats (Friday supper to Sunday afternoon); occasional non-meditation weekend workshops (music, yoga, natural building).
about: Wattle Hollow Retreat Center is a small, hand-built meditation retreat property on 40 wooded acres near Devil's Den State Park in Northwest Arkansas, founded and directed by Joy Fox, a longtime student of S.N. Goenka, Jack Kornfield, Ruth Denison, and other Insight Meditation teachers. The land, developed by Fox over more than three decades and dotted with cob-built structures such as the 'Crystal Palace' and 'Cob Castle,' hosts monthly silent one-day Dharma Days of Theravada Vipassana sitting, walking, and metta practice, as well as periodic two-night Friday-to-Sunday weekend meditation retreats. Retreats are held in Noble Silence with group discussion periods, and an organic vegetarian lunch is served. Visiting teachers also lead occasional non-meditation weekend programs in yoga, Vajrayana study, and music, but the core recurring offering is Vipassana meditation practice. All meditation retreats and Dharma Days are offered free of charge in the dana tradition, at a property with capacity for about 20-25 guests.
schedule: Recurring one-day Dharma Days (10am-4pm) of sitting, walking, and metta meditation in Noble Silence; periodic Friday-evening-to-Sunday-afternoon weekend meditation retreats; occasional weekend workshops from visiting teachers.
cost: All meditation retreats and Dharma Days are offered free of charge (dana/donation-based, per Buddhist tradition); no one is turned away for lack of funds.

pricePerDay.notes: Strictly donation-based with no suggested amount; retreatants may offer dana via Zelle, PayPal, or Venmo after the retreat.

foodNotes: An organic vegetarian lunch is served during Dharma Days; weekend retreats begin with a shared Friday supper and include meals through Sunday.
workNotes: No work practice is required of meditation retreatants; separate natural-building ('cobbing') workshops are a distinct, optional activity offered at other times.
